tagline: A celebrated car-free island served today by two competing panga operators — ready for a quieter premium tier.
summary: Isla Holbox is a car-free island at the north of the Yucatán, famous for its quiet sand streets, bioluminescence and whale-shark season. Every visitor arrives by boat across the Chiquilá channel, today on panga-style ferries that run roughly every 30 minutes across two operators. On a short, high-frequency, island-only crossing with no road alternative, a faster, quieter premium tier is a natural fit.

journeys.name: Chiquilá ↔ Isla Holbox
journeys.today: A ~30-minute panga crossing every half hour, packed in high season.
journeys.with_navier: A smooth, quiet premium hop to a car-free island with no road alternative.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Pioneer II owns the Chiquilá↔Holbox crossing (~5 nm) comfortably inside all-electric range.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Quanta-LR (H2 2026+) is optional here; the core network is well inside Pioneer II all-electric range.

competitive_landscape: Two panga operators (Holbox Express, 9 Hermanos) split the crossing; no foiling or premium tier exists — the pain is crowding and wait times in peak season.
seasonality: Atlantic hurricane season (Jun–Nov) is the constraint; whale-shark season (roughly May–Sep) is peak. The lagoon channel is short and sheltered.
regulatory_note: Mexican jurisdiction: API Quintana Roo and the Capitanía de Puerto (SEMAR). Clean-fleet operation aligns with the Yum Balam protected area around Holbox.

internal.posture_note: Car-free island, single high-frequency crossing, no road alternative
